parts.note: reads as a description of loving fondness, but literally describes holding someone tightly in your arms

explanation.definitionFit: To hug someone fondly is to hold them close out of affection.

parts.note: the transport hangs from an overhead wire as it carries passengers up a mountain

explanation.definitionFit: A gondola-style vehicle hangs from a wire rope and carries skiers or tourists up slopes.

parts.note: a catch can be a snag in a deal or a device that snares; here the snare kills

explanation.definitionFit: A dangerous place or vehicle likely to kill is a lethal snare, a catch with fatal results.

definitions.meaning: a dense grey chemical element, symbol Pb, used for weights
the principal performer in a show, taking the top role

explanation.definitionFit: Pb is a famously dense metal, and the performer in the top role is the principal one in the cast.

parts.note: suggests postal addresses for the mail, but means formal talks that a speaker delivers

explanation.definitionFit: Formal addresses are talks given to an audience, and one delivers a talk.

parts.note: sounds like a regimental flag-bearer, but describes the board an artist mixes paints on

explanation.definitionFit: An artist's board holds the paints, the colours, during painting.

clue.text: No longer one scolds, but rather frees from blame

parts.note: ex- describes something former, as in an ex-wife
to rate someone is an old word for berating or scolding them

explanation.surface: Someone no longer scolds a person and instead clears them of guilt.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE meaning to scold is an old verb, related to berate.
explanation.definitionFit: To exculpate is to clear someone of guilt, declaring them blameless.

indicators.note: the clue's words provide the answer from within themselves, the letters running across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A woman named Bertha, if asked, will supply a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Look across 'BertHA IF Asked' for the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This Israeli city on the Mediterranean is a major seaport.

clue.text: He is taken in by a bearded Indian chief of the desert

indicators.note: the pronoun is received inside the following description, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Sikh men traditionally leave their beards uncut
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man is welcomed into the home of a bearded Indian, an Arab leader.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab tribal leader of the desert peoples carries this title.

clue.text: Something like a rush on silver is accepted

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece goes on top of, after, the first

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a reed is a tall waterside grass similar to a rush

explanation.surface: A sudden demand for silver is generally approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' suggests a run on a market, but here it is the marsh plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something agreed upon has been consented to by all parties.

clue.text: Plea for one to be agreeable and provide financial backing

definitions.text: Plea for one to be agreeable and provide financial backing

parts.words: Plea for one to be agreeable and provide financial backing
parts.note: a polite request meaning please be kind, plus the theatrical sense of a wealthy backer

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a coaxing request for kindness, and a theatrical backer who funds a show is called an angel.

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: turned about, the word for sinful is read from its end

parts.note: evil means wicked or sinful

explanation.surface: A woman described as wholly free of sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinful about' looks like a description of a person; 'about' here turns the word round, and 'her' is the definition, standing for a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's forename, so it can stand for a woman referred to as her.

parts.note: suggests a considered remark, but describes sound bounced back off a surface, repeating the speaker

explanation.definitionFit: Sound reflected off a wall repeats the speaker's words back.

clue.text: A gamekeeper might, if the bag isn't good enough!

definitions.text: A gamekeeper might, if the bag isn't good enough!

parts.words: A gamekeeper might, if the bag isn't good enough!
parts.note: the bag is the day's shoot of game; a poor tally might lead to the keeper being dismissed

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be dismissed from a job, with the bag and sack both evoking a holder for game.

definitions.meaning: to stop and detain someone to talk to them
a flower worn in the lapel slot of a jacket

explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone and keep them talking is to detain them; a lapel flower such as a rose shares the name of the lapel slot.

clue.text: Giving frolicsome dog a run on the beach

indicators.note: playful and capering, so the letters romp into a new order

explanation.surface: Letting a playful dog have a run along the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frolicsome' rearranges DOG, A and RUN. 'On the beach' means stranded, as a ship run onto the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship stranded on the shore or shallows is stuck, beached.

clue.text: Gets full satisfaction out of religious work

parts.note: ex is Latin for from or out of
the Acts of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: Someone finds complete fulfilment from doing church work.
explanation.definitionFit: To demand and obtain what is fully due is to get complete satisfaction of a claim.

definitions.meaning: traders must regularly count their inventory
thieves in a shop literally carry off goods

explanation.definitionFit: Taking inventory is a retailer's duty, while thieves literally remove the goods.

parts.note: to credit a story is to believe it

explanation.surface: Someone convinced that money will please a certain man.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic gold. Read whole, the clue describes the person owed money, whom payment would satisfy.
explanation.definitionFit: A lender owed money is satisfied when the debt is paid, perhaps in gold.

clue.text: Very accurate spinners brought back on

indicators.note: brought back means the word for spinners is read in reverse

parts.note: tops are spinning toys

explanation.surface: Spin bowlers recalled to the attack with precision.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exactly right is precisely correct.

clue.text: No one takes part — it's most offensive

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
some means a part or portion of something

explanation.surface: Nobody joins in, because the thing is so repellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most' here intensifies, as in 'most kind', rather than forming a superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a foul smell or character is extremely unpleasant.

clue.text: Small cask for fresh water-or sea-water?

definitions.meaning: a small keg carried on a boat for drinking water
a wave that crashes on the shore

explanation.definitionFit: Sailors' small water keg has this name, and a crashing wave on the shore shares it.

definitions.meaning: locked with a sliding bar on a door
ran off suddenly, like a horse

explanation.definitionFit: A door locked with a bar is secured; a horse that runs off suddenly has fled.

clue.text: Servant turns in during dinner, perhaps

parts.note: dinner is one example of a meal

indicators.note: turns means the little word in is turned round

explanation.surface: A servant takes a turn at the table during dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Servant turns in' reads as a servant going to bed; really 'turns' flips the little word and 'during' sets it within the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic doing lowly work is a household servant.

clue.text: German city circulating a list of necessities

indicators.note: circulating suggests the letters move around into a new order

explanation.surface: A German city sends round a checklist of basic needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating' rearranges A and LIST to TIALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic requirements that cannot be done without are fundamentals.

clue.text: Rent a seaside place in Yugoslavia

definitions.meaning: a tear or rip, a noun here
a port on the Dalmatian coast, now in Croatia

definitions.meaning: put to work, consumed for a purpose

explanation.definitionFit: Pre-owned goods are previously owned; something employed rather than squandered has been put to service.

clue.text: Some misleading description of man, say

explanation.surface: A rather deceptive account of humanity.

explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, so that word describes it.

parts.note: reads as protection against snow, but means a shelter built out of snow

explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit dome house is built of blocks of packed snow.

parts.note: describes going past a target or runway end by accident

explanation.definitionFit: Going past a target or runway by mistake is going too far.

clue.text: I need to think, and I want to look

definitions.meaning: a phrase said while pausing to consider
a request to be shown something

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is uttered while pondering, and also when asking to be shown something.

definitions.meaning: a lip-spouted glass container in a laboratory
